payload-written-as-plain-json-data.text: Payload written as plain JSON: data.
Fields, relationships and validation. The table of the mapping itself is in the spec; where each type lives is in the modules model.

relationships.text: A stored payload is a Plutus data value. The plain mapping is a partial function from JSON to data; the plain reading is a partial function from data to JSON.

Reading after mapping is the identity on accepted JSON, compared as JSON values (numbers by value, objects without order). Mapping after reading is the identity on data that has a plain reading. Together the image of the mapping and the domain of the reading are the same set.
The entry arguments carry the schema beside the payload file's path. A command with no payload file ignores it.

validation.text: A number is accepted when its value is a whole number with at most 1000 digits. A number with a large exponent is judged by its size before it is expanded.
A text is accepted whatever it holds; it is stored as its UTF-8.
An object's keys are sorted by their UTF-8 bytes before the entries are listed.
With the plain schema a whole document that the detailed schema accepts is refused before the mapping runs.

state.text: None. No file, journal entry or on-chain value gains a field.
